'''Anne E. Carpenter''' is an American scientist in the field of image analysis for [[cell biology]] and [[artificial intelligence]] for [[drug discovery]]. She is the co-creator of [[CellProfiler]], open-source software for high-throughput biological image analysis, and a co-inventor of the [[Cell Painting]] assay, a method for image-based profiling. She is an Institute Scientist and Senior Director of the Imaging Platform at the [[Broad Institute]] and a professor in the Departments of Biological Sciences and Computer Science in the Institute of [[Physical artificial intelligence|Physical AI]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.broadinstitute.org/imaging|title=Broad Institute Imaging Platform|date=2016-01-08|website=Broad Institute|language=en|access-date=2019-02-02}}</ref>

== Education and early career ==
=== Undergraduate training ===
Carpenter received her B.Sc. in Biological Sciences in 1997 from [[Purdue University]], West Lafayette.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ibiology.org/speakers/anne-carpenter/|title=Anne Carpenter • iBiology|website=iBiology|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> During this time, she spent a summer in 1996 as an [[HHMI]] Undergraduate Research Fellow in the laboratory of Robert E. Malone at the [[University of Iowa]], working on the control of recombination in [[yeast]]. Following her graduation, she spent a summer working on [[enhancers]] in [[Drosophila]] neural development as a research assistant in the laboratory of [[Chris Q. Doe]], then at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]].

=== Graduate training ===
Carpenter carried out research for her Ph.D. in the laboratory of Andrew S. Belmont at the [[University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign]]. There, she developed molecular biology and automated imaging systems to rapidly assess the effects of [[transcriptional activator]]s  on large-scale [[chromatin]] structure using [[fluorescence microscopy]]. This work laid the foundation for studies of engineered regions of the [[genome]], the movement of genes within the [[Cell nucleus|nucleus]] upon gene activation, and chromatin-related high-throughput screens. She received her PhD in cell biology in May 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iridescentlearning.org/2018/02/computational-drug-discovery-an-interview-with-dr-anne-carpenter/|title=Computational Drug Discovery: An Interview with Dr. Anne Carpenter|date=2018-02-09|website=Iridescent|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mcb.illinois.edu/news/feature/122|title=Profile: Anne Carpenter {{!}} The School of Molecular and Cellular Biology {{!}} University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|website=mcb.illinois.edu|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

=== Post-doctoral training and creation of CellProfiler software ===
Carpenter trained in the laboratory of [[David M. Sabatini]] at the [[Whitehead Institute]] for Biomedical Research, Cambridge MA, during her postdoctoral work (July 2003 to December 2006). Through co-mentoring by [[Polina Golland]], professor at [[MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory]], Carpenter transitioned into a computational researcher during this time. Her research focused on high-throughput microscopy and living cell [[microarrays]] to reveal gene function. This required new image analysis methods, so Carpenter and collaborator Thouis Jones designed and in 2005 released the first open-source high-throughput cell image analysis software, [[CellProfiler]], which was first published in 2006.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=CellProfiler: image analysis software for identifying and quantifying cell phenotypes|journal=Genome Biology|volume=7|issue=10|pages=R100|date=2006-10-31|language=en|doi=10.1186/gb-2006-7-10-r100|pmid=17076895|pmc=1794559|last1=Carpenter|first1=Anne E.|last2=Jones|first2=Thouis R.|last3=Lamprecht|first3=Michael R.|last4=Clarke|first4=Colin|last5=Kang|first5=In|last6=Friman|first6=Ola|last7=Guertin|first7=David A.|last8=Chang|first8=Joo|last9=Lindquist|first9=Robert A.|last10=Moffat|first10=Jason|last11=Golland|first11=Polina|author11-link=Polina Golland|last12=Sabatini|first12=David M. |doi-access=free }}</ref> Using this new tool, she led a team of 5 researchers to develop advanced [[data mining]] methods to systematically examine the necessity of proteins for a variety of biological processes.

== Research and impact ==
In January 2007, Carpenter founded her laboratory at the [[Broad Institute]] of Harvard and MIT, as the Director of the Imaging Platform. Her first [[NIH]] R01 grant was awarded in 2010, at the age of 33. In 2017, she became a Broad Institute Scientist.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.broadinstitute.org/people/institute-scientists|title=Broad Institute Scientists|website=Broad Institute|date=21 June 2017|language=en|access-date=2019-02-21}}</ref>

The Carpenter group develops novel strategies and tools to analyse biological images, particularly microscopy images from high-throughput experiments. Her [[computer scientists]] and [[biologists]] develop free [[open-source]] image analysis and data exploration methods such as [[CellProfiler]] and CellProfiler Analyst. Their software work has contributed to open source applications and libraries, including [[ImageJ]], [[TensorFlow]], [[scikit-image]], and [[scikit-learn]]. The lab collaborates with biologists, generating discoveries across fields of study and disease areas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.research.gov/research-portal/appmanager/base/desktop;jsessionid=xq6TT1ZTQPqX28QpDks0y0RyBDxnL9HFZrN2QBcHVL31V3dCnwQV!648838783!-468424801?_nfpb=true&_windowLabel=awards_1&_urlType=action&wlpawards_1_id=/researchGov/AwardHighlight/PublicAffairs/2013/24202_Miningcellularimages.html&wlpawards_1_action=selectAwardDetail|title=Mining cellular images|website=Research.gov|language=en|access-date=2019-02-21}}</ref> Their software enables [[high-throughput screening]] in challenging model systems such as [[C. elegans]], 3D cell cultures, and time-lapse video of growing cells.

The focus of the Carpenter lab turned towards [[machine learning]] by 2009, and later [[deep learning]], to identify biological structures of interest and to identify patterns resulting from chemical or genetic perturbations to identify cures for diseases. She was an early pioneer of the new field of image-based profiling,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.352.6288.877|title='Cell painting' highlights responses to drugs and toxins|date=2016-05-20|journal=Science|doi=10.1126/science.352.6288.877|language=en|access-date=2019-02-02|last1=Pennisi|first1=E.|author-link=Elizabeth Pennisi|volume=352|issue=6288|pages=877–878|pmid=27199393|bibcode=2016Sci...352..877P|url-access=subscription}}</ref> which is related to [[gene expression profiling]] but uses microscopy images as the data source. Together with [[Stuart Schreiber]], the Carpenter laboratory invented the [[Cell Painting]] assay,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Multiplex Cytological Profiling Assay to Measure Diverse Cellular States|journal = PLOS ONE|date=2013-12-02|language=en|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0080999|volume=8|issue = 12|article-number=e80999 | last1 = Gustafsdottir | first1 = Sigrun M. | last2 = Ljosa | first2 = Vebjorn | last3 = Sokolnicki | first3 = Katherine L. | last4 = Wilson | first4 = J. Anthony | last5 = Walpita | first5 = Deepika | last6 = Kemp | first6 = Melissa M. | last7 = Petri Seiler | first7 = Kathleen | last8 = Carrel | first8 = Hyman A. | last9 = Golub | first9 = Todd R. | last10 = Schreiber | first10 = Stuart L. | last11 = Clemons | first11 = Paul A. | last12 = Carpenter | first12 = Anne E. | last13 = Shamji | first13 = Alykhan F.|pmid = 24312513|pmc = 3847047|bibcode = 2013PLoSO...880999G|doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Cell Painting, a high-content image-based assay for morphological profiling using multiplexed fluorescent dyes|date=2016-08-25|language=en|pmc=5223290|pmid=27560178|doi=10.1038/nprot.2016.105|volume=11|issue=9|journal=Nat Protoc|pages=1757–74 | last1 = Bray | first1 = MA | last2 = Singh | first2 = S | last3 = Han | first3 = H | last4 = Davis | first4 = CT | last5 = Borgeson | first5 = B | last6 = Hartland | first6 = C | last7 = Kost-Alimova | first7 = M | last8 = Gustafsdottir | first8 = SM | last9 = Gibson | first9 = CC | last10 = Carpenter | first10 = AE}}</ref><ref>{{cite bioRxiv |last1=Seal |first1=Srijit |title=A Decade in a Systematic Review: The Evolution and Impact of Cell Painting |date=2024-05-07 |language=en |biorxiv=10.1101/2024.05.04.592531 |last2=Trapotsi |first2=Maria-Anna |last3=Spjuth |first3=Ola |last4=Singh |first4=Shantanu |last5=Carreras-Puigvert |first5=Jordi |last6=Greene |first6=Nigel |last7=Bender |first7=Andreas |last8=Carpenter |first8=Anne E.}}</ref> which is the most widely used for this purpose. Carpenter's CellProfiler software and Cell Painting assay formed the initial scientific platform for Recursion Pharmaceuticals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/the-subtle-art-of-really-big-data-recursion-maps-the-body/|title=The subtle art of really big data: Recursion Pharma maps the body|last=Ray|first=Tiernan|website=ZDNet|language=en|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> Dr. Carpenter is a member of the Scientific and Technical Advisory Board for Recursion Pharmaceuticals,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.recursionpharma.com/team-member/anne-carpenter/|title=Anne Carpenter|website=Recursion Pharmaceuticals|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> in addition to that of [[Bio-Rad Laboratories]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.recursionpharma.com/press-release/recursion-pharmaceuticals-announces-formation-scientific-technical-advisory-board/|title=Recursion Pharmaceuticals Announces Formation of its Scientific and Technical Advisory Board|website=Recursion Pharmaceuticals|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>

Carpenter has given more than 200 invited lectures and has chaired several [[conferences]] and workshops. She has authored over 200 scientific publications as of 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=UOYBbDYAAAAJ&hl=en&authuser=2|title=Anne Carpenter Google Scholar profile|website=Google Scholar|language=en|access-date=2022-09-11}}</ref> She is known for efforts that organize the scientific community: she was an early Board member for the Society for Biomolecular Imaging and Informatics (SBI2), she founded the CytoData Society, and she led the 2018 Data Science Bowl via Kaggle.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kaggle.com/c/data-science-bowl-2018#About|title=2018 Data Science Bowl|website=Kaggle|language=en|access-date=2019-02-21}}</ref> Since 2007, Carpenter has supervised over 70 researchers and students, from [[postdoctoral]] to high-school level and is known for her informal mentoring as well.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/science/comments/7xpwc0/science_ama_series_dr_anne_carpenter_institute|title=Carpenter Reddit AMA|date=2018-02-15|website=Reddit|language=en|access-date=2019-02-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/DrAnneCarpenter|title=Carpenter Twitter feed|website=Twitter|language=en|access-date=2019-02-21}}</ref>

In 2021, Dr. Shantanu Singh became co-leader of Carpenter's laboratory, now called the Carpenter{{ndash}}Singh lab.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Carpenter |first1=Anne E |title=Why I shrank my lab by half |journal=eLife |date=5 September 2022 |volume=11 |article-number=e82831 |doi=10.7554/eLife.82831|pmid=36063089 |pmc=9444239 |doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2026, Carpenter has returned to Purdue as a professor. <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bio.purdue.edu/news/articles/2026/anne-carpenter-returns-to-purdue-as-professor-bringing-pioneering-expertise-in-computational-biology-and-imaging.html}}</ref>
